test_title: SSC Selection Post HSC Level Official Paper (Held on: 4 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If O is the orthocentre of a ∆ ABC and ∠BOC = 140°, then the measure of ∠BAC is:
solution:
**GIVEN:**

A triangle ABC and O is orthocentre 

angle BOC = 140^circ 

**CONCEPT USED:**

Sum of all the angles in quadrilateral = 360 degree

Orthocentre : It is the point where the perpendicular drawn from the vertices to the opposite

sides of the triangle intersect each other 

**CALCULATION:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb8937eb80be8b7f5f2606b5d21f2f53beb92ffca5530c49391dc12aa0b6ecb5.png] 

If in triangle ABC, BE and CD are altitudes and they intersect at O then,

 angleODA = angleOEA = 90 and angleBOC = angleDOE = 140 

 In quadrilateral ADOE 

⇒ angle ADO + angleDOE + angleOEA + angleDAE = 360 

⇒ 90 + 140 + 90 + angle DAE = 360 

⇒ angleDAE = 360 - ( 90 + 140 + 90) = 360 - 320 = 40 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] 

__Shortcut Trick__**

 angleBOC + angleBAC = 180 

⇒ angleBAC = 180 - 140 = 40 

**Hence, the required angle is 40 degree.**
